_meta.indication: EOVIST Injection is a gadolinium-based contrast agent indicated for intravenous use in T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the liver to detect and characterize lesions in adults with known or suspected focal liver disease.

pivotal_trials.design: Blinded-read study in which patients underwent non-contrast MRI followed by gadoxetate-contrasted MRI, read independently by three blinded readers; Test = Pre + Post Eovist Contrast MRI vs Primary Comparator = Pre-Contrast MRI.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with known or suspected focal liver lesions scheduled for liver surgery (mostly malignant lesions).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was the lesion detection rate (Test vs Comparator difference in per-patient numbers of lesions detected).
pivotal_trials.n: 172 patients enrolled, 169 dosed, 131 in the per-protocol (preferred) efficacy analysis.
pivotal_trials.result: Success criterion met: average detection rate for all lesions Test = 79% vs Comparator = 74%, CI for difference (0%, 10%); the marginal superiority was traced to improved detection in patients with multiple (clustered) lesions (Test 64% vs Comparator 55%).

pivotal_trials.design: Blinded-read detection study (identical protocol to A03779), read independently by three blinded readers; Test = Pre + Post Eovist Contrast MRI vs Primary Comparator = Pre-Contrast MRI.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with known or suspected focal liver lesions scheduled for liver surgery (mostly malignant lesions).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was the lesion detection rate.
pivotal_trials.n: 169 patients enrolled, 162 dosed, 131 in the per-protocol (preferred) efficacy analysis.
pivotal_trials.result: Success criterion met: average detection rate for all lesions Test 78% vs Comparator 74%, CI for difference (0%, 8%); superiority driven by clustered lesions (Test 67% vs Comparator 62%).

pivotal_trials.design: Blinded-read characterization study with three independent blinded readers; Test = Pre + Post Eovist Contrast MRI vs Primary Comparator = Pre-Contrast MRI.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients scheduled for contrast biphasic spiral liver CT with a broader range of focal liver lesion types.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was the lesion characterization rate (proportion of SOR lesions correctly characterized).
pivotal_trials.n: 235 patients enrolled, 231 dosed, 182 in the per-protocol analysis.
pivotal_trials.result: Success criterion met: average correct classification all lesions Test = 67% vs Comparator = 54%, CI for difference (9%, 17%); characterization superiority achieved primarily on benign lesions (Test 86% vs 77%).

pivotal_trials.design: Blinded-read characterization study (identical protocol to A05742) with three independent blinded readers; Test = Pre + Post Eovist Contrast MRI vs Primary Comparator = Pre-Contrast MRI.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients scheduled for contrast biphasic spiral liver CT with a broader range of focal liver lesion types.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was the lesion characterization rate (proportion of SOR lesions correctly characterized).
pivotal_trials.n: 240 patients enrolled, 235 dosed, 177 in the per-protocol analysis.
pivotal_trials.result: Success criterion met: average correct classification all lesions Test = 68% vs Comparator = 58%, CI for difference (6%, 14%); benign lesions Test 79% vs Comparator 71%.

key_safety: Overall 4.3% of subjects reported one or more adverse reactions; most common were feeling hot (0.9%), nausea (0.6%) and headache (0.5%). Serious class-associated risks are nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF) and anaphylactoid/hypersensitivity reactions.
target_moa: Gadoxetate disodium is a paramagnetic gadolinium-based T1 MR contrast agent that shortens the T1 relaxation time of hydrogen protons, increasing signal intensity on T1-weighted images; a lipophilic (EOB) moiety allows uptake into hepatocytes via membrane-bound carriers (OATP) with excretion into bile by an organic anion transporter.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for Nephrogenic Systemic Fibrosis (NSF): gadolinium-based contrast agents increase the risk for NSF in patients with acute or chronic severe renal insufficiency (GFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2) or acute renal insufficiency due to hepato-renal syndrome or the perioperative liver transplantation period; avoid use unless diagnostic information is essential.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the product is a member of the previously approved class of gadolinium-based contrast agents and did not pose unique concerns.

description.text: Added pediatric use findings (ages >2 months to 18 years) for MRI of the liver to labeling section 8.4

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application proposes to add the clinical findings from an observational study in pediatric age group greater than 2 months to 18 years in section 8.4 of the package insert in fulfillment of a PMR from July 2008 approval letter.

summary.text: Standard NDA (505(b)) for a new molecular entity gadolinium-based MRI contrast agent; approved first cycle on the basis of four Phase III blinded-read trials, with no advisory committee convened and PREA pediatric and 505(o) NSF postmarketing requirements.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated June 29, 2007, received July 2, 2007, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Eovist® (Gadoxetate Disodium) Injection.
Chemical class: This product is new molecular entity (NME).

Your application for Eovist® Injection was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because your product is a member of the class of previously approved gadolinium-based contrast agents and the product did not pose unique concerns beyond those applicable to other members of this class.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric study under PREA for MRI of the liver in pediatric patients ages 0 to 2 months with known or suspected hepatobiliary pathology, obtaining evaluable safety and imaging data from at least 10 subjects.

citations.quote: - Deferred pediatric study under PREA for use in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the liver in pediatric patients ages 0 to 2 months with known or suspected hepatobiliary pathology. This study will obtain evaluable safety and imaging data from at least 10 subjects, however, due to the anticipated rarity of these clinical conditions in this pediatric population, progress towards recruitment will be assessed at one year after study start and the targeted number of patients may require adjustment. Any adjustment in the sample size will be supplied in a protocol amendment that contains supportive information and a request for FDA concurrence. Descriptive statistics will summarize safety and efficacy outcomes. Efficacy determination will be based upon extrapolation from studies in other patient populations.

requirement.text: Deferred PREA observational study of Eovist in pediatric patients aged >2 months to 18 years referred for routine contrast-enhanced liver MRI for suspected or known focal liver lesions, obtaining evaluable safety and imaging data from at least 50 subjects.

citations.quote: 2. To conduct the study entitled, "An observational study of the administration of Eovist® in pediatric patients who are referred for a routine contrast enhanced liver MRI because of suspected or known focal liver lesions." This study will enroll subjects aged > 2 months to 18 years and obtain evaluable safety and imaging data from at least 50 subjects. Efficacy will be assessed based upon comparison of uncontrasted images to Eovist®-contrasted images. Descriptive statistics will summarize safety and efficacy outcomes.

requirement.text: Required postmarketing clinical trial under 505(o) to collect clinical data sufficient to assess the magnitude of risk for development of NSF among patients with moderate (GFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2) to severe renal insufficiency.

citations.quote: 3. A trial to collect clinical data sufficient to assess the magnitude of risk for the development of NSF with your product among patients with moderate (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73m2) to severe renal insufficiency.

requirement.text: Single-center crossover study to evaluate the possible influence of erythromycin as an example of an OATP inhibitor on hepatocyte uptake of Eovist in liver MR imaging in healthy subjects.

citations.quote: 4. To conduct a single center crossover study to evaluate the possible influence of Erythromycin as an example of an inhibitor of the organic anion transporting peptide on the hepatocyte uptake of Eovist® in liver MR imaging in healthy subjects.
